gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Storybook nostalgia with a modern backbone. Mystery Quest is at its best in open-jawed curves and compact ascenders, while Noto Sans Kaithi, a sans-serif, fills the line with lowercase that stands like capitals.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Noto Sans Kannada, a friendly sans-serif, rises gently from small letters to capitals, with s curves opening wide at both ends. Mystery Quest brings a bookish, nostalgic display voice to the top.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Mystery Quest arrives bookish and nostalgic, with open-jawed curves. Noto Sans Lepcha, a sans-serif with wide curve openings and a lowercase tall as cast iron capitals, makes the pair feel sturdy yet inviting.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Noto Sans Mandaic runs curvy and unclamped, its lowercase nearly capital height. Mystery Quest brings bookish, nostalgic display character with open-jawed curves, and the body text happily stays out of its way.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Bookish nostalgia lives in Mystery Quest and its open-jawed curves. Noto Sans Meroitic does the quiet job, with c openings you can see through and lowercase that fills the line like capitals.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Storybook looks, modern manners: Mystery Quest leads with open-jawed curves and compact ascenders. And Noto Sans Old Hungarian, a sans-serif with large counters, keeps apertures open even when sized tiny.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Storybook nostalgia meets chunky clarity: Mystery Quest curls open-jawed and compact, while Noto Sans Old Turkic stands tall. That sans-serif body keeps curves open while the heading sets the mood.
gen-nixie-one-gf-orbit: Retro-tech nostalgia in one constant stroke. Nixie One is strongest at showing that look with open curves, while Orbit, a sans-serif, is best at floating each character apart on rope-like stems.
